newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, July 7 - CPO production in June was in line with our estimate of 780-785,000 tonnes which we had maintained throughout the month. Production practically stagnated at an estimated 785,000 tonnes as against a rise of 7.6 percent to 790,600 tonnes in May. Compared to June last year, production grew nearly 9 percent. For the 3 months ended June. Production expanded strongly by 12 percent and exceeded the first-quarter growth of 7.8 percent. Production in January-June totalled an estimated 4.07 million tonnes. This is 10.2 percent or about 380,000 tonnes more than the corresponding period of last year.

Meanwhile, the weather has improved in the last 10 days with increased rainfall in most crop areas. We expect the seasonal uptrend in production to resume this month. Production for the whole year now looks likely to comfortably surpass our May 7 projection of 8.8 million tonnes. Palm oil offtake also slackend off in June with exports estimated to have shrunk to 595,000 tonnes as against our previous estimate of around 615,000 tonnes and 626,600 tonnes in May. Increased offtake of some 45,000 tonnes by China as more than offset by the sharp cutback of an estimated 135,000 tonnes in shipments to India and Pakistan.

However, competition in the export market is going to be more keen because of increased export availabilities of edible oils in the coming months. Almost ideal growing weather conditions coupled with a 10.4 percent expansion in SB planted accreage to 70.85 million accres in the U.S. is likely to result in a bin-busting harvest of 2.8 billion bullish this season or 17.5 percent more than 1996-97. Planting of the Indian groundnut crop has also got off to a good start, particularly in Gujerat. Good price and timely arrival of monsoon had encouraged farmers to expand acreage under the oilseed.

CBT Soya price fell sharply in recent weeks with the July and September SB contract dropping 137.5 cents and 92.75 cents to $7.22 and $6.18 per bullish respectively between June 13 and July 13. September SBO futures fell 1.35 cents/LB ($29.74/NT) to 22.35 cents after posting a life-of-contract closing low of 21.73 cents on July 1. Canola price also sank to life-of-contract lows. CPO futures lost 53-45 ringgit in the five days ended June 30 before staging a modest rebound of Friday July 4. The September contract settled at 1,167 ringgit after posting an intra week low of 1,142 ringgit.

Heavy buying by one leading CPO producer-refiner, especially og August/September RBD Palm olein, helped to stem the decline in price but traders with long positions and refiners who were undersold were quick to sell. We see limited scope for further price gains and feel the market is more vulnerable to resuming its downtrend. It lost 90-63 ringgit in June.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
